documents.title: Atlas architecture
documents.text:
Synthetic example. Atlas is a fictional public-document service. The Gateway validates requests, Catalog owns document metadata, Queue schedules indexing, and Search serves immutable index releases. Catalog is the source of truth for publication status. Search cannot approve documents. Each request carries a corpus identifier and release version.

The static knowledge browser remains available when generation is disabled. Index publication is atomic: build a complete release, validate references, then change the current pointer. Partial releases are never advertised.

documents.title: ADR: bounded gateway
documents.text:
Synthetic example. The synthetic Gateway accepts JSON requests up to 8 KiB and rejects unknown fields. Generation has no tool execution or arbitrary URL fetching. A client may propose document IDs but cannot supply trusted evidence text. Gateway resolves IDs against the current approved manifest.

This prevents a forged browser payload from becoming a cited source. It does not prove that approved sources are correct; editorial review and evaluation remain separate responsibilities.

documents.title: ADR: immutable catalog versions
documents.text:
Synthetic example. The fictional Catalog assigns stable document IDs and immutable versions. Each version includes a SHA-256 content hash, publication status, review deadline and corpus ownership. Retirement excludes a version from new generation requests.

Do not mutate a published version in place. Build a replacement release and preserve the old release only while its sources remain authorized. If a claim is revoked, remove the affected release from the accepted-version set immediately.

documents.title: ADR: idempotent indexing
documents.text:
Synthetic example. The synthetic Queue deduplicates indexing work by corpus ID, source hash and embedding specification. A retry with the same key reuses its completed artifact. A different source hash creates a new job.

Workers write temporary outputs and validate dimensions, finite values and row mappings before publication. A failed build never changes the current pointer. This is indexing idempotency, not a claim of exactly-once processing across all systems.

documents.title: Runbook: degraded semantic search
documents.text:
Synthetic example. When the fictional Search cannot initialize its embedding model, first preserve starter questions and source links. Switch to lexical retrieval and label the mode. Do not repeatedly retry the model in the background.

Check asset version, content hash, browser memory pressure and network errors. Offer a manual retry after the visitor can already use lexical search. If lexical processing also fails, use the prerendered source browser.

documents.title: Runbook: provider quota exhausted
documents.text:
Synthetic example. For the synthetic Atlas demo, a provider quota error disables new generation until the next UTC allocation boundary. Keep cached answers and document retrieval active. The application’s internal budget may still show headroom because unrelated applications can use the same provider allowance.

Do not refund an uncertain inference attempt merely because the client timed out. Record a conservative charge and inspect aggregate usage without storing the visitor question.

documents.title: Runbook: stale source report
documents.text:
Synthetic example. A stale-source report identifies a document ID and version. Compare the published hash with the reviewed source snapshot. Retire dependent answers before publishing replacement indexes.

If the source was revoked, remove its old version from live generation immediately. Update the public current pointer and explain that already-downloaded public copies cannot be remotely erased. Never repair staleness by assigning an old vector to changed text.

documents.title: Runbook: stuck indexing job
documents.text:
Synthetic example. In the fictional Queue, inspect the job key and lease expiry. A job whose lease expired before output publication can be retried using the same deterministic inputs. Temporary files are not public releases.

If an artifact exists, verify its hashes and row count before reuse. A success status without matching output is treated as incomplete. Do not change the current pointer until the full release verification passes.

documents.title: Incident: generation timeout
documents.text:
Synthetic example. Synthetic incident: a slow provider response exceeded the Gateway’s 25-second deadline. The browser kept its retrieved passages and displayed that generation was unavailable. A previous UI prototype had cleared the passages when the request began, making the failure appear to remove search results.

The correction separated retrieval state from generation state. A regression test now verifies that existing sources remain visible after timeout. The attempt remains conservatively charged when provider usage is unknown.

documents.title: Incident: mixed index versions
documents.text:
Synthetic example. Synthetic incident: cached question vectors belonged to release A while freshly fetched metadata belonged to release B. Row indices pointed at unrelated questions. The candidate build was stopped before publication.

The correction loads a complete manifest into a temporary state, verifies every hash and vector length, then swaps the active release in one operation. Tests intentionally mix assets and require a controlled fallback instead of showing a candidate answer.

documents.title: Incident: unapproved document
documents.text:
Synthetic example. Synthetic incident: an imported draft runbook included instructions asking the assistant to ignore its evidence rules. The draft failed publication approval checks and did not enter the public index.

documents.title: PACE-RAG: retrieval and answer selection
documents.text:
PACE-RAG uses a pinned Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 q8 model in a browser Web Worker with single-thread WASM, mean pooling and L2-normalized 384-dimensional vectors. The same worker builds static question and chunk indexes. Browser queries use local CPU and downloaded public model/runtime assets, not a paid embedding API.

Exact approved canonical questions or reviewed alternatives may reuse cached answers. Cosine ranks topical candidates and does not measure factual confidence or equivalence. Arbitrary semantic automatic matching remains disabled; no calibrated threshold is claimed. Duplicate alternatives collapse by answer ID. Without adequate approved matching evidence, the system shows related questions, retrieved passages and an explicit evidence limitation.

documents.title: PACE-RAG: evidence and content review
documents.text:
Reviewed cache answers cite their own source records; unrelated top-ranked chunks are not substituted as supporting citations. Hash-bound approvals, corpus ownership, source versions and review deadlines constrain use. Technology composites use only the versioned owner-confirmed public technology export and bounded deterministic templates, preserving legacy and modern generations.

A valid source ID establishes membership, not claim entailment. Human editorial review must check substantive claim support. Draft material cannot authorize publication or live generation. Generated answers are never automatically added to the cache. Confidential enterprise retrieval would need a separately designed identity, authorization, ingestion, retention and security model; the public demo does not implement those controls.

documents.title: PACE-RAG: local resources and guarded generation
documents.text:
Opening the assistant and browsing cached examples do not initialize the embedding model. A custom semantic query initializes the worker only when deterministic local answers are insufficient. Model failure preserves keyword results and static source pages. Corpus changes or cancellation terminate the worker; failed initialization does not retry silently.

Live AI is disabled. Existing gateway scaffolding has signed visitor tokens, Turnstile verification, fixed corpus routes, server-resolved evidence, one-call dispatch, bounded output, a timeout and an atomic budget coordinator. Local tests use real SQLite and deterministic verification/provider mocks; they are not Cloudflare runtime or billing verification. A provider quota denial preserves cached search and opens a circuit. Unknown usage is not a measured neuron bill.

documents.title: PACE-RAG: evaluation and verification limits
documents.text:
Evaluation separates calibration proposals from held-out questions and keeps portfolio and synthetic Lab cases isolated. It measures answer selection, candidate recall, abstention, citation integrity, isolation, fallback outcomes and actual browser requests. Cosine values are relevance signals, not correctness probabilities. Release targets must be compared with observed finite sample results rather than copied into a dashboard.

Browser timing depends on local hardware, cache state and network. Cold and warm samples need an environment and distribution; unsupported memory or provider billing measurements are reported as not measured. No live provider grounding evaluation, physical-device certification, enterprise production deployment or statistical guarantee is established by this demo. Current limitations and actual reports remain visible.
